headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify LlamaFactory outputs into unsafe actions and data exposure, while LlamaFactory itself is inert.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest MCP/tool outputs, browser content, and files, so prompt injection is plausible in default web-dev setups. LlamaFactory is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it is not itself a bridge; the risk comes from open-webui parsing untrusted content that could steer downstream prompts or tools.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to any MCP/OpenAPI tool server or browser-sourced content is fed into prompts
IF operators copy LlamaFactory-generated text into open-webui without sanitization
mitigations: Disable tool use for untrusted chats
Add a system prompt that treats all retrieved content as untrusted
Require manual review before any tool call
Separate LlamaFactory outputs from open-webui prompt context
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for retrieved content

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches files, persistent memory, API keys, and broad external services by default, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network surfaces. If LlamaFactory artifacts or training data are placed into open-webui’s workspace, open-webui can transmit them to third parties or retain them in memory, creating a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory artifacts, datasets, or logs are mounted into open-webui’s local files or data volume
IF open-webui is configured to use external APIs or search connectors on those files
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory data outside open-webui mounts
Turn off external connectors for sensitive chats
Rotate or remove exposed API keys immediately
Use a separate workspace per agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or egress network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. open-webui can write to local files and mounted volumes, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority in the profiles, making direct capability conflict limited.
conditions: IF open-webui and another process share the same mounted volume for writes
IF operators manually grant LlamaFactory write or network permissions not shown in the profile
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Mount LlamaFactory data read-only
Avoid shared git worktrees
Check container permissions before launch
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can treat upstream content as chat context and then act through tools, APIs, or browser sessions; LlamaFactory can generate model outputs that may be copied into that context. Because open-webui has downstream action authority and no verification guarantee is documented, errors can cascade from LlamaFactory outputs into real actions.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory outputs are pasted or imported into open-webui as authoritative context
IF open-webui is allowed to call tools, send messages, or browse based on that context
mitigations: Require human verification before tool execution
Mark LlamaFactory outputs as untrusted drafts
Disable autonomous actions in open-webui
Use a review-only workflow for generated content
requires-engineering: add validation gates before side effects

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, usage analytics, persistent memory, and files, while LlamaFactory is an open-source local tool with no stated compliance controls. The pair creates a mismatch risk if regulated data is routed into open-webui’s broader retention and third-party service paths; LlamaFactory is not cited for residency because its profile shows no such controls.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are entered into open-webui
IF open-webui retention, analytics, or external API paths are enabled for that data
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in open-webui chats
Disable analytics for sensitive deployments
Review retention settings before use
Store secrets in a dedicated vault
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
